title: Octaves and middle C
summary: The same note name comes back higher and lower. Octave numbers tell you which one is meant.

steps.title: Same name, higher or lower
steps.body:
Play a C, then the next C to the right. They sound like the same note, one higher than the other. That jump is an **octave**.

Every note name repeats once per octave. A tune played an octave higher is still the same tune.

steps.title: Octave numbers
steps.body:
To say which C you mean, add a number. Middle C is **C4**. The C above it is C5 and the C below it is C3.

The number goes up at every C, not at A. So the B just below middle C is B3, and the D just above it is D4.

steps.title: C3, C4 and C5
steps.body: Three Cs, one octave apart. The middle one is middle C, C4.

items.prompt: Play C5, the next C up.
Play C3, the C below middle C.
Play G4, the G just above middle C.
Play B3, the B just below middle C.

steps.title: Move it up and down
steps.body: Play the same tune in two different octaves. It is the same tune, just higher or lower. The app shows the octave number on each note you play.

items.prompt: Find B4, the last white key before C5.
